body: Housing allowance: the monthly housing allowance cap is EUR 2,500 per month for a standard relocating employee. The housing cap is paid against a signed lease.
Housing allowance city tier: the monthly housing cap rises to EUR 3,200 per month in tier-1 cities. City-tier housing cap adjustment applies to the standard housing allowance.
Housing allowance eligibility: the monthly housing cap applies for the first 12 months of the assignment. Housing allowance requires a registered lease in the employee name.
Housing deposit: the company advances the rental security deposit, repaid from the housing allowance over the assignment.
Relocation allowance: the one-time relocation allowance is a lump sum of EUR 5,000 paid to cover miscellaneous moving costs. The relocation allowance is a single payment.
Relocation allowance payment timing: the one-time relocation allowance is paid in the first payroll cycle after the start date. Relocation allowance is paid once.
Relocation allowance tax: the one-time relocation allowance is treated as taxable income and grossed up by the company.
Home leave: the policy covers two home-leave trips per year for the assignee. Home-leave trips are economy round-trip flights to the home country.
Home leave family: home-leave trips cover the employee and accompanying dependants once per year. Additional home-leave for family is at employee cost.
Home leave travel class: home-leave flights are booked in economy class for trips under six hours and premium economy above. Home-leave class follows the travel policy.
Education allowance: the policy covers international school tuition up to EUR 20,000 per child per year. School tuition is reimbursed against invoices.
Education allowance age: school tuition coverage applies to children aged 4 to 18. Schooling support ends when the child reaches 18.
Education enrolment fees: one-time school enrolment and registration fees are reimbursed in addition to the annual tuition cap.
School transport: daily school bus transport is reimbursed up to EUR 1,500 per child per year under the education allowance.
Tax equalization: under tax equalization the assignee pays a hypothetical home-country tax and the company covers all actual host and home taxes. Tax equalization keeps the assignee tax-neutral.
Hypothetical tax: the hypothetical tax under tax equalization is deducted each payroll based on the employee's home-country liability. Hypo tax is the assignee's only tax cost.
Tax equalization true-up: an annual tax-equalization true-up reconciles hypothetical tax against actual tax after filing. The true-up settles any balance with the company.
Tax provider: the company appoints a tax provider to prepare home and host filings for assignees under tax equalization.
Household goods shipment: the policy covers a household goods shipment of up to 40 cubic metres by sea freight. The HHG shipment volume cap is per family.
Air freight allowance: an additional air-freight household goods shipment of up to 100 kg is covered for immediate-need items. Air freight supplements the sea shipment.
Shipment insurance: the household goods shipment is insured at replacement value during transit. HHG shipment insurance is arranged by the mover.
Temporary accommodation: serviced temporary accommodation is provided for up to 30 days on arrival. Temporary accommodation bridges the gap before the permanent lease starts.
Temporary accommodation standard: temporary accommodation is a one-bedroom serviced apartment, upgraded to two-bedroom for families. The standard follows family size.
Temporary accommodation extension: an extension of temporary accommodation up to 15 additional days may be approved by HR if the permanent home is delayed.
Language training: the policy includes up to 60 hours of host-country language training for the employee. Language training is delivered by an accredited provider.
Language training family: the accompanying spouse is eligible for 40 hours of language training. Family language training supports settling in.
Language training format: language training may be taken in person or online and must start within the first six months of the assignment.
Spousal support: the policy provides a spousal career support allowance of EUR 5,000 for job-search and accreditation costs. Spouse support is a one-time benefit.
Partner support services: the spouse receives CV, networking and job-search coaching from a partner-support provider. Spousal support services run for six months.
Spouse work permit: the company sponsors the spouse work-permit application where the host country allows dependant employment.
Immigration support: the company sponsors and pays for the employee's work visa and residence permit. Immigration support is handled by an appointed law firm.
Immigration dependants: dependant visas and residence permits for the spouse and children are covered under immigration support. Dependant immigration is arranged together with the employee.
Immigration renewal: the first work-permit renewal during the assignment is covered by the immigration support benefit.
Repatriation: at the end of the assignment the policy covers a return household goods shipment equivalent to the outbound shipment. Repatriation shipment volume matches the inbound cap.
Repatriation flights: one-way return flights to the home country for the employee and dependants are covered on repatriation. Repatriation flights follow the home-leave travel class.
Repatriation reintegration: a reintegration allowance of EUR 3,000 supports the move back home. Repatriation reintegration is paid on return.
Per diem: a settling-in per diem of EUR 80 per day is paid during the temporary-accommodation period. Per diem covers meals and incidentals.
Per diem duration: the settling-in per diem is paid for the first 14 days after arrival. Per diem stops once the permanent home is occupied.
Per diem family uplift: the per diem is increased by EUR 30 per day per accompanying dependant during settling-in.
Relocation flights: one-way relocation flights to the host country are covered for the employee and accompanying dependants. Relocation flights are booked by the company travel desk.
Relocation flight class: relocation flights are economy for short-haul and premium economy for flights over six hours. Flight class follows the travel policy.
Relocation baggage: extra checked baggage on relocation flights is reimbursed up to EUR 300 per traveller.
Storage: the policy covers storage of household goods for up to 60 days during the move. Storage bridges shipment and permanent-home availability.
Storage cost cap: household goods storage is reimbursed up to EUR 1,500 total. The storage cap applies per relocation.
Storage location: storage may be at origin or destination and is arranged by the appointed moving company.
Cost of living allowance: a cost-of-living allowance (COLA) is paid when the host location index exceeds the home index. COLA is calculated from an independent cost-of-living index.
COLA review: the cost-of-living allowance is reviewed every six months against the latest index. COLA may rise or fall on review.
COLA basis: the cost-of-living allowance applies to a defined spendable-income portion of base salary, not the full salary.
Health insurance: the company provides international private health insurance for the assignee for the assignment duration. Health insurance covers inpatient and outpatient care.
Health insurance dependants: the international health insurance covers the spouse and children as dependants. Family health coverage matches the employee plan.
Health insurance emergency: the international health plan includes emergency medical evacuation and repatriation cover.
Miscellaneous allowance: a miscellaneous settling-in allowance of one month's salary covers incidental setup costs. The miscellaneous allowance is a lump sum.
Miscellaneous allowance scope: the miscellaneous allowance covers utility connections, driving-licence conversion and small appliances. Miscellaneous allowance needs no receipts.
Miscellaneous allowance timing: the miscellaneous settling-in allowance is paid with the first host-country payroll.
Intern relocation: interns and graduate hires receive a flat relocation lump sum of EUR 1,500. The intern relocation package is reduced versus the standard policy.
Intern housing: interns receive shared housing or a housing stipend of EUR 800 per month, below the standard housing cap. Intern housing support is time-limited.
Intern flights: a single economy relocation flight to the host country is covered for interns. Intern flights exclude dependants.
